topSignals.title: Nebius confirms 328 MW Bloom SOFC deployment at Vineland NJ — Bloom +13%, FCEL +11%, NBIS +20%
topSignals.text: — During Nebius Group Q2 2026 earnings (August 12), management confirmed it replaced previously planned combustion-based power with 328 MW of Bloom Energy SOFCs at its flagship Vineland, New Jersey AI data center. CCO Tom Blackwell: the switch "significantly enhanced the project" from a community perspective; Andrey Korolenko (Chief Product & Infrastructure): "Bloom fuel cells deployment should be fast." Nebius beat Q2 expectations and set a 5 GW contracted-power target by end-2026, with Bloom partnership expected to "unlock and expedite" additional sites. Bloom rose 13% to ~$391 (new record), FCEL climbed 11% on sympathetic buying, and NBIS surged 20%+ on earnings. 247wallst | Nebius PR | DCD | Investing.com

topSignals.title: FERC RM26-4: T-4 days — no tariff filings confirmed yet
topSignals.text: — The August 17 hard deadline for PJM, MISO, NYISO, and SPP compliance filings arrives Monday. As of August 13, no conforming tariffs have been published to the FERC docket. These submissions will define the new large-load interconnection cost structure across approximately 70% of US electrical load — the direct regulatory basis for the $5-20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost LCOE input. CAISO remains on a November compliance track; ISO-NE's "Bring Your Own Generation" mandate for new large-load data centers is still pending. FERC RM26-4 | Akin Gump

topSignals.title: Goldman Sachs adds Ceres Power to August European Conviction Buy list — 168% upside forecast
topSignals.text: — Goldman Sachs retained its Buy rating on Ceres Power (CWR.L) and elevated it to the August European Conviction List (highest-confidence buy calls), assigning Ceres the largest forecasted gain on the roster at approximately 168%. GS characterises Ceres's licensed SOFC stack technology as a key solution for AI data centre power supply and frames the July 2026 share-price pullback as a buying window. Context: CWR.L had already gained +446% in the prior 12 months as of July 1, 2026. TheStreet

Nebius / Bloom Energy — 328 MW Vineland NJ (UPDATED): See Top Signal #1. First US site now identified as Vineland, NJ; combustion infrastructure replaced with Bloom SOFCs to address permitting, zoning, and community opposition. Previously listed in carry-forward as pipeline; now confirmed active deployment. Nebius 5 GW power target by end-2026 implies further Bloom SOFC tranches expected.

Active pipeline carry-forward (unchanged): Oracle Project Jupiter (2.45 GW, Sep 14 NMED hearing); Crusoe/Cheyenne (900 MW Phase 1, first data halls H2 2026); Hedgehog USA Texas (1.5 GW, Phase 1 104 MW pre-construction); FCEL/Fit Energy (380 MW total, 30 MW delivery H2 2026); Equinix >100 MW (19+ DCs); Bloom/Brookfield $25B EaaS framework; ECL/PowerCell 300 MW+ H2 (Jul 14, Bosch-backed); MiTAC Fremont AI campus islanded microgrid.
FERC RM26-4 — T-4 days to August 17: See Top Signal #2. The single most important near-term date for US on-site SOFC LCOE economics. Monitor FERC docket for Monday filings.

Background unchanged: NY EO 62 data center moratorium (50 MW+, islanded exemption active); Germany EnEfG PUE <=1.2/ERF >=10%/15% waste heat from July 2026; EU CADA energy efficiency rating scheme delayed; ITC 48E 30% credit active for all fuel cell feedstocks; ERCOT Batch Zero self-supply active; 8 US states with enacted data center tax restrictions.

Rolls-Royce SMR (UK): GDA Step 3 completion expected August 2026 — no formal ONR announcement confirmed as of August 13. If published, marks a regulatory milestone relevant to European co-location markets and SOFC's longer-horizon competition.
Holtec / EDF / Tritax (UK): First European SMR-powered data center planned in Nottinghamshire (June 2026 announcement, no August update). Lead times 10+ years.

Background unchanged: 13 hyperscaler nuclear deals totalling >9.8 GW; nuclear 10+ year lead times remain the primary SOFC competitive differentiator for near-term deployment. Battery storage at ~$25/MWh LCOE unsuitable for 24/7 AI baseload.

[First citation] SOFC-LiBr/H2O absorption trigeneration parametric analysis (Fuel Cells, Vol 26, Issue 2, 2026; e70092; Mouissi et al.; correction note August 11) — Energy and exergy analysis of a combined SOFC + LiBr-H2O single-effect absorption chiller system. Parametric investigation of current density, fuel utilization, operating temperature, and pressure effects on electrical output, thermal recovery, and cooling performance. Second-law (exergy) evaluation of overall system. LCOE-model relevant: quantifies how SOFC waste heat can drive absorption cooling to replace electric chiller draw, improving effective net electrical efficiency in DC heat-management scenarios — directly applicable to the absorption chiller PFD (INOCEL System_Architecture, Aug 12) and SOFC-CHP sensitivity inputs. Wiley Fuel Cells

[First citation] "Recent developments in control and integration of solid oxide fuel cells: From stack to system" (Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, 2025; pii S1364032125006732) — Systematic review of SOFC control strategies and system integration from 2020-2025: load-following, thermal management, dynamic response, and balance-of-plant integration. System-level focus; useful for assessing control architectures for data-center SOFC deployments. Not LCOE-model relevant directly but informs dynamic operation assumptions. ScienceDirect

lcoe.text: FERC RM26-4 (T-4 days): August 17 PJM/MISO/NYISO/SPP filings will convert the $5-20/MWh avoided-transmission-cost benefit from an estimate to a defined tariff input. Activate as a live LCOE sensitivity lever once filings land.

Nebius EaaS pricing anchor: The original Nebius-Bloom MoU (May 2026) covered up to 328 MW under a multi-year EaaS framework. The August 12 confirmation of active deployment at Vineland NJ validates that behind-the-meter EaaS pricing is sufficient to displace combustion infrastructure commercially. No per-kWh figure disclosed publicly; monitor SEC filings and Nebius earnings transcripts for PPA/EaaS rate disclosure.

SOFC-LiBr trigeneration efficiency gain: SOFC + absorption chiller integration can meaningfully reduce net electrical draw for cooling vs. compressor-based DC cooling (quantified in Mouissi Fuel Cells 2026); model as a positive correction to effective electrical efficiency in the LCOE sensitivity tool's CHP/heat-credit scenario.

Background carry-forward unchanged: US natural gas $4.00-4.90/MMBtu (EIA 2026); SOFC commercial system capex $4,000-6,000/kW (target $1,000/kW); ITC 48E reduces effective capex to $2,800-4,200/kW; CCGT $2,000-2,200/kW; solar+battery $25/MWh LCOE (24/7 baseload-unsuitable).
